nodes.text: Let $\alpha$ be an irrational number. Is it true that if, for all large $n$,\[\#\{ 1\leq m\leq n : \{ \alpha m\} \in [u,v)\} = n(v-u)+O(1)\]then $u=\{\alpha k\}$ and $v=\{\alpha \ell\}$ for some integers $k$ and $\ell$?

#998 : [Er64b,p.61] analysis | diophantine approximation A problem of Erdős and Szüsz. Hecke [He22] and Ostrowski ( [Os27] and [Os30] ) proved the converse. This is true, and was proved by Kesten [Ke66] .
